notes.meaning: The Lord rules over the whole world as its true King. His earthly throne was above the gold winged figures, called cherubim, on the ark of the covenant. Because He is so great and holy, all nations and peoples should stand in deep awe before Him.

The Lord chose Zion, the hill of Jerusalem where His temple stood, to reveal His special presence among His people. Even though He made His home with Israel, His power reaches far beyond them. He stands supreme above every nation on earth.

All people are called to praise God's name because it inspires wonder and reverence. To say God is holy means He is completely pure, set apart from all evil, and like no one else. This holiness is the main reason all creation owes Him worship.

Earthly rulers often abuse their strength, but the Lord always uses His mighty power to do what is fair and right. He set up just laws for the descendants of Jacob. His kingdom brings true justice because He always defends what is good.

Worshippers are invited to bow low before God's footstool, which usually meant the sacred chest called the ark of the covenant inside the tabernacle and temple. Believers must approach Him with great humility. We lift Him high in praise because He alone is completely pure and holy.

differ.view: The footstool refers to the earthly temple and ark, designed to lift believers' minds past physical objects to God in heaven and protect them from worshiping material things.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The footstool is taken as the human flesh of Christ, born of Mary, which Christians rightly worship because His human nature is united to His divine person.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Because the ark was missing after the exile during the second temple era, the footstool likely refers to the temple building itself or Mount Zion.

notes.meaning: Moses, Aaron, and Samuel are remembered as faithful leaders who pleaded with God for Israel. Moses served as a priest before Aaron's family was set apart, and Samuel was famous for his powerful prayers. Whenever these men cried out to the Lord, He heard and answered them.

God guided His people by speaking from the cloudy pillar during their journey through the wilderness. These leaders listened closely and obeyed the laws and commands He gave them. Their lives show that God listens to those who faithfully keep His word.

The Lord showed great mercy by answering their prayers and forgiving the nation instead of destroying them. At the same time, He sent loving discipline for their wrong choices so they would not treat sin lightly. His mercy and His justice always work hand in hand.

The song ends with a final call to praise the Lord and worship Him at His holy hill of Zion. Calling Him our God reminds His people that this great King is also in a close covenant relationship with them. His absolute holiness is the ultimate reason to honor Him with our whole lives.
